claims.title: Why do all the matrix entries lie in one finite extension?
claims.hypotheses: The compact group has a continuous finite-dimensional representation over an algebraic closure of ℚℓ and a finite initial coefficient field may be prescribed.
claims.statement: There is one finite extension of ℚℓ containing every matrix entry of the representation, including those of inverses. It can contain the prescribed field.

claims.title: Which lattice records an integral combination of group matrices?
claims.hypotheses: A compact group acts continuously on a finite-dimensional vector space over a finite extension E of ℚℓ.
claims.statement: The ℤℓ-span of the group matrices is a finite free algebra containing the identity, generated as a module by finitely many group matrices. Its left action is continuous in integral coordinates.

claims.title: How much trace precision forces divisibility in the matrix lattice?
claims.hypotheses: The global representation is semisimple over the algebraic closure of ℚℓ. Divisibility is taken in the integral span of its group matrices.
claims.statement: A fixed nonnegative loss c suffices for all n. If every translated trace belongs to ℓⁿ⁺ᶜ𝒪_E, then the matrix belongs to ℓⁿM.

claims.title: Why does one extra binary digit determine membership in the lattice?
claims.hypotheses: The cyclic group of order two acts on ℚ₂² through the identity and the sign matrix diag(1,−1).
claims.statement: On the lattice with basis I,D the two translated traces of aI+bD equal 2a and 2b. The least uniform precision loss is one binary digit.

claims.title: How does one trace approximation give a map of lattices?
claims.hypotheses: Finite weighted families of continuous auxiliary representations of the target rank approximate the semisimple target character uniformly at every precision. Coefficients can lie in a ramified finite extension and may be nonintegral.
claims.statement: Each sufficiently accurate family gives a full integral lattice in its product of matrix spaces and a comparison to the target lattice modulo the prescribed power of ℓ, with a weighted trace estimate.

claims.title: Which maps are compatible when the precision increases?
claims.hypotheses: For every precision, the finite lists, coefficient fields and stable lattices have been chosen compatibly on repeated entries. The auxiliary depths can be enlarged.
claims.statement: Nondecreasing depths and nested tuples give exactly equivariant transitions. Comparison with the fixed lattice commutes modulo ℓⁿ. At each precision the target quotient is covered.

claims.title: What are the local representations in a rationalized layer?
claims.hypotheses: At the local group each auxiliary is semistable, with specified filtration multisets at all embeddings in all admitted finite coefficient models. A crystalline conclusion at a level additionally requires crystalline auxiliaries.
claims.statement: The rationalized levels are sums of column representations over ℚℓ. They inherit semistability and the uniform filtration window. Under the separate period-limit theorem, evaluation on the identity transfers the period condition to the target.

claims.title: How do filtration jumps become exponents in a period matrix?
claims.hypotheses: One rationalized layer is de Rham. Its period filtration equals the whole invariant space at −H and is zero at H+1. A generator of the maximal ideal in the positive de Rham period ring is fixed.
claims.statement: A filtration-adapted invariant basis has period matrix W diag(uʰʲ) with W invertible over the positive period ring. The exponents admit a common nonnegative shift and satisfy |pⱼ−q|≤H.
